report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**, not false. Scientific evidence demonstrates that bystander hands-only (compression-only) CPR is associated with significantly greater survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest compared to receiving no bystander CPR.

### Key Findings
* **Increased Overall Survival:** Observational studies and population registries confirm that both compression-only CPR and conventional CPR lead to substantially higher survival rates than no bystander intervention (https://www.mdedge.com/ehospitalistnews/article/18117/trauma/compression-only-cpr-increased-cardiac-arrest-survival).
* **Doubled Survival Rates:** Data from the American Heart Association indicates that performing CPR immediately can double or triple a cardiac arrest victim's chance of survival (https://cpr.heart.org/en/resources/cpr-facts-and-stats). Large-scale registry studies similarly show that survival chances double with any form of bystander CPR compared to no CPR (https://medicalxpress.com/news/2019-04-compression-only-cpr-survival-out-of-hospital-cardiac.html).
* **Favorable Patient Outcomes:** Clinical research shows that patients receiving bystander compression-only CPR consistently achieve better clinical outcomes and higher survival rates than those receiving no CPR (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-27096-9?error=cookies_not_supported&code=c4f5f5e4-21e8-48cb-b407-c90f12e714ba).
